Murtaugh Family KitchenLethal WeaponTwo partners. One family dinner.Every recipe serves 4.
    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersRiggs' trailer snacksCrackers and whatever's left in his fridgeHow to make it250g sharp cheddar150g sliced salami1 sleeve saltine cracker1 jar pickled jalapeñosCut the cheddar into slabs and fold the salami into quarters.Lay them out on a chopping board with the saltine crackers and a small bowl of pickled jalapeños. Eat straight off the board.Christmas party crab dipMurtaugh house at ChristmasHow to make it250g cream cheese, softened150g sour cream2 tsp Worcestershire sauce1 lemon200g crab meat100g cheddar, grated200g crackersHeat the oven to 190°C. Mix the cream cheese, sour cream, Worcestershire and a squeeze of lemon.Fold in the crab and half the cheddar, spoon into a dish and top with the rest.Bake until bubbling.Serve with crackers.Trish's honey butter dinner rollsThe Murtaugh family tableHow to make itAs written, serves 4Soft milk bread rolls proved twice and baked golden, brushed with melted honey butter and finished with flaky salt, served warm in a basket.Warm 250ml milk with 40g butter and 2 tbsp caster sugar to blood heat, then add 7g dried yeast and 1 egg.Mix into 500g bread flour with 1 tsp salt and knead 8 minutes.Prove 1 hour until doubled.Shape into 12 balls in a greased tin and prove 30 minutes more.Bake at 190°C for 18 minutes.Melt 30g butter with 1 tbsp honey, brush over the hot rolls and sprinkle with flaky salt.MainsBrown sticky stew, done rightThe family jokes about her cooking, make yours betterHow to make it1kg diced beef chuck2 tbsp neutral oil1 onion2 carrots2 celery sticks2 tbsp tomato paste250ml red wine500ml beef stock4 sprigs of thyme1kg potatoes60g buttersalt and pepper, to tasteSeason the beef with salt and pepper and brown it in the neutral oil in batches.Soften the chopped onion, carrots and celery, then stir in the tomato paste.Add the wine, stock and thyme and return the beef.Braise in a 150°C oven.Boil the potatoes towards the end of braising and mash with butter. Serve the stew on top.Not the world's worst turkey and stuffingRiggs finally gets invitedHow to make itAs written, serves 4Brined turkey breast roasted juicy, with sage cornbread stuffing, roast sweet potato and a proper pan gravy.Brine a 1.5kg turkey breast overnight in 2 litres water with 100g salt and 50g brown sugar.Pat dry, rub with butter and roast at 170°C for about 75 minutes until it reads 70°C inside, then rest 15 minutes.Mix 300g crumbled cornbread with 1 diced onion and 2 celery sticks softened in butter, chopped sage, 1 egg and 200ml stock, and bake 30 minutes.Roast 800g sweet potato wedges alongside.Make gravy from the pan juices, 1 tbsp flour and 300ml stock.SweetsRoger's birthday cakeFifty candles, he's too old for thisHow to make it200g butter, softened, for the cake250g caster sugar4 eggs250g self-raising flour50g cocoa, for the cake200ml milk200g butter, softened, for buttercream300g icing sugar40g cocoa, for buttercream1 packet birthday candlesHeat the oven to 170°C and line two tins. Beat the butter for the cake with the sugar, then add the eggs.Fold in the flour, the cocoa for the cake and the milk and divide between the tins.Bake until a skewer comes out clean.Cool the cakes completely.Beat the butter, icing sugar and the cocoa for the buttercream.Fill, cover and add candles.DrinksRiggs' beach trailer micheladaIce-cold lager mixed with lime, hot sauce, Worcestershire and tomato juice in a chilli salt-rimmed glass, finished with a lime wedge.How to make it2 tbsp salt1 tsp chilli powder2 limes1 tray ice120ml lime juice240ml tomato juice16 dashes of hot sauce8 dashes of Worcestershire sauce4 bottles of cold lager (375 ml)Mix the salt and chilli powder on a plate. Rub the glass rims with lime and dip.Fill the glasses with ice and add lime juice, tomato juice, hot sauce and Worcestershire.Top with cold lager poured slowly, stir once and garnish with lime wedges.
